title: Water for a School in Asonsuaso: From First Visit to Handover
alt: Ribbon-cutting at the completed school water installation
intro: A visit can reveal a need. Returning to meet that need is where the work begins. In 2026, Good God Charity Foundation followed a school water project in Asonsuaso through its initial assessment, construction, progress, and final handover. The project is now complete and has been handed over.

chapters.title: 01 · Before the work began
paragraphs: Before there was a handover ceremony, there was a conversation about water. In the initial film, a representative of the school explains that she had been asked to keep pupils away from a community borehole. Her account brings the need into focus: access to water was a concern in the children’s school day.

For pupils, the school day should be a time to learn, take part, and grow. Water supports the ordinary routines around that learning—drinking, washing, and caring for the shared school environment. Hearing the school’s concern gave GGCF a practical direction for its response: a water installation on the school grounds.

The foundation’s next step was to return and carry that response through. The project grew from a visit and a conversation into work at the school itself. That connection between listening and acting is where this story begins.
chapters.caption: The school setting in Asonsuaso, shown in the initial project film.

chapters.title: 02 · Turning a decision into work
paragraphs: The next chapter moves from the visit to the work itself. Construction photographs show people mixing material, moving it by wheelbarrow, and working around the new structure beside the school building. These are the practical steps behind a finished project—the work that has to happen before a ribbon can be cut.

The camera stays close to that process. The school remains in the background while the installation takes shape in the foreground. The project’s purpose and its setting stay connected: this is work being carried out where the school community will use it.
chapters.caption: Construction beside the school building, documented during the project.

chapters.title: 03 · Staying with the process
paragraphs: A separate progress film carries the story beyond the start of the job. Together with the construction photographs, it records the middle of the journey: the period between deciding to help and being ready to hand over the result.

That middle chapter matters. A completed installation is the result of work carried through, rather than a single day of activity. Keeping a record of the stages allows supporters to follow the project as it develops and connects the final ceremony to the effort that came before it.

chapters.title: 04 · A completed project, handed over
paragraphs: In the final film, the foundation returns to the school for the handover. People gather beside the completed water installation. A pink ribbon is cut at the tiled structure, with the installation’s blue filter housing visible nearby. The occasion brings the story back to the school community, where it began.

The project has been completed and handed over. That is the milestone at the heart of this story: a need recognised during a visit has become an installation delivered at the school. The four films preserve that journey—from the first look at the setting to the work, the progress, and the final ceremony.

For GGCF, giving is expressed through practical action and follow-through. This project adds a lasting piece of infrastructure to that work. Its handover closes the construction chapter and begins the next one: the facility’s place in the daily life of the school.
chapters.caption: The ribbon-cutting ceremony, shown in the final project film.

title: Christmas Support at Missionaries of Charity Sisters
alt: GGCF volunteers arranging donated supplies at Missionaries of Charity Sisters
intro: In December 2025, Good God Charity Foundation brought its giving campaign to Missionaries of Charity Sisters in Ashtown-Mbrom, with a focus on supporting children with special needs.

chapters.title: Coming together to give
paragraphs: The campaign invited supporters to join a donation visit on 20 December 2025. Its focus was children with special needs in the care of Missionaries of Charity Sisters. The invitation placed practical generosity at the centre of the Christmas season: coming together to support children and the people caring for them.

The event photographs show GGCF volunteers arranging a broad collection of supplies. Bottled water and drinks, packaged food, tissue products, bedding, and other bundled items are visible around the donation table. Each part of the collection reflects the same purpose: bringing useful support to the home.

chapters.title: Practical care, shared with love
paragraphs: The visit continued GGCF’s commitment to supporting vulnerable children through direct action. At the centre of the story are the children, their carers, and a group of people willing to contribute what they could.
This Christmas outreach forms another chapter in the foundation’s work: turning a public invitation to give into supplies brought to the people the campaign was created to support.

title: Supporting Pupils at New Amakom Primary School
alt: GGCF volunteer sharing items with pupils during the New Amakom school visit
intro: In December 2024, Good God Charity Foundation visited New Amakom Primary School. The outreach brought volunteers and pupils together for a donation event centred on practical support and personal connection.

chapters.title: Meeting pupils where they learn
paragraphs: The photographs place this story at the school itself. Pupils gather around the volunteers as items are shared, while other pictures capture groups of children in front of the New Amakom school building. The visit brought the foundation’s work into the setting where the pupils spend their school day.

The donation was also an opportunity to spend time with the children. The images record conversation, attention, and moments shared between pupils and volunteers. That personal connection is part of GGCF’s approach to giving: responding to practical needs while showing care for the people behind them.
chapters.caption: Pupils pictured outside New Amakom Primary School during the outreach.

chapters.title: Another step in supporting education
paragraphs: The school visit added an education-focused chapter to the foundation’s earlier orphanage and healthcare donations. It reflected the same commitment to bringing support to children in the places that care for and educate them.
The photographs preserve the people and setting of that day. Together, they tell the story of a school community visited, pupils engaged, and support shared.
